scope: Shared-source bridge evidence for hemp phenotyping, plant-experiment metadata, germplasm identity, chemistry identity, and flowering genetics.
rules: Shared source identities are mapped only to scoped claims and do not approve a full lesson.
Database identity evidence is distinct from biological-effect evidence.
Government and standards records remain version- and retrieval-context dependent where fields are volatile.
Existing lesson publication and review states remain unchanged.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Plant phenotyping evidence is more reusable when biological material, environment, treatments, observation variables, methods, and data context are recorded in a structured way.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: MIAPPE v1.2 release and standard fields for plant phenotyping experiment metadata.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports the encyclopedia evidence framework and its requirement to preserve context around measurements and experiments.
claimEvidence.limitations: MIAPPE is a metadata standard; it does not validate a cultivation target or prove a biological relationship.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: A germplasm accession is a controlled identity record with passport and repository context and should not be treated as interchangeable with an informal cultivar or market strain name.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: USDA GRIN-Global Cannabis taxon/accession records and Cornell/USDA-ARS hemp germplasm repository program description.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports distinctions among accession, cultivar, line, clone, and displayed name.
claimEvidence.limitations: Repository identity does not by itself prove genetic uniformity, ownership, commercial naming equivalence, or current availability.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Flowering behavior in hemp can have major genetic determinants; the cited dissertation reports two major flowering-time loci on chromosome 1 named Autoflower1 and Early1.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Toth 2022 Cornell dissertation abstract and dissertation p. ii, as preserved in the reviewed Grow Doc claim record.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports the lesson's treatment of autoflowering/day-neutral phenotypes as genetically influenced rather than purely environmental labels.
claimEvidence.limitations: The mapped loci are study- and germplasm-specific evidence and are not sufficient to predict flowering behavior in every Cannabis genotype.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Limonene discussion should distinguish a chemically identified compound record from cultivar aroma labels or inferred biological effects, using stable compound identity where possible.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: PubChem PUG REST compound-domain and CID property-table specification.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports chemical-identity discipline for the limonene lesson and downstream Terpene Atlas records.
claimEvidence.limitations: PubChem establishes database identity and properties; it does not establish limonene abundance in a plant sample or a cannabis-specific physiological or human effect.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Beta-caryophyllene records should use stable chemical identifiers and stereochemistry-aware structure data rather than relying only on a common-name string.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: PubChem PUG REST compound identifiers and property-table interface.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports chemical-identity discipline for beta-caryophyllene and shared chemistry tooling.
claimEvidence.limitations: Chemical identity does not establish concentration, sensory prominence, dose, pharmacology, or cannabis-specific biological effect.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Seed and germplasm conservation records should preserve accession identity and repository/passport context so regeneration, characterization, and distribution remain traceable.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: USDA GRIN-Global Cannabis germplasm records and Cornell/USDA-ARS hemp germplasm repository program description.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports the lesson's identity and documentation requirements for germplasm backup and regeneration.
claimEvidence.limitations: These sources do not provide one universal storage interval or regeneration threshold for every seed lot; lot-specific viability and storage evidence remain necessary.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Morphology and growth measurements are more comparable when trait definitions, units, timing, biological material, and measurement methods are controlled and recorded.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: USDA Hemp Phenotyping and Protocol Handbook v4 descriptor/protocol framework plus MIAPPE v1.2 observation metadata structure.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports standardized plant-height, stem, flowering-time, biomass, and related measurement records.
claimEvidence.limitations: Specific descriptor methods and units must remain tied to the applicable handbook version and experiment design; they are not universal performance targets.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Experimental conclusions are more interpretable when study design, biological material, environment, treatments, observation variables, and data files are described together.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: MIAPPE v1.2 plant phenotyping experiment metadata model.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports the lesson's requirement to document controls, replication, treatments, material identity, and observation context.
claimEvidence.limitations: MIAPPE structures metadata and does not by itself determine whether replication is statistically adequate or a causal conclusion is justified.
